title: CPR
text: Start compressions at once if there is no normal breathing: heel of the hand on the centre of the chest, 100 to 120 per minute, 5 to 6 cm deep, full recoil between pushes.
Give 30 compressions then 2 rescue breaths; keep going with minimal pauses.
Attach the AED as soon as it arrives, follow its voice prompts, and clear the person before any shock.
Do not stop except to swap rescuers, follow the AED, or on signs of life. Hand over to the crew medical officer.
In microgravity, first restrain the patient on a rigid surface such as the Crew Medical Restraint System; an unrestrained patient drifts away with every compression.
Use a microgravity method: the Evetts-Russomano method for basic life support, or the handstand method against the opposite wall with the patient restrained for advanced life support.
Keep the Earth targets: 100 to 120 compressions per minute, about 5 cm deep, with full recoil.
Do not use the recovery position; restrain the person so they cannot drift, and turn the head to the side if vomiting.

inflight.note: This variant follows the microgravity guideline; in partial gravity (Moon base, rover) use the Earth steps above.
